title: Morse Inequalities and the Handle Chain Complex

items.title: Morse numbers and the Morse polynomial
items.statement: Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold and $f:M\to\mathbb R$ a Morse function. For every integer $k$ the **Morse number** $m_k(f):=\#\{p\in\operatorname{Crit}(f):\operatorname{ind}(p)=k\}$ is a finite nonnegative integer, and $m_k(f)=0$ unless $0\le k\le n$. The **Morse polynomial** of $f$ is $M_f(t):=\sum_{k=0}^{n}m_k(f)t^k\in\mathbb Z[t]$, a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients and $M_f(1)=\#\operatorname{Crit}(f)$. The index is the number of negative squares of the Hessian in the library's convention. The definition is purely geometric: no field, coefficient ring, or orientation enters, and the empty and zero-dimensional cases are included.
items.strategy: Definition. It packages the critical points of a Morse function by index using the published Morse definitions, and it is well posed because a Morse function on a compact manifold has only finitely many critical points (published corollary) and because the index of a nondegenerate critical point is an integer in $[0,n]$. Nothing is proved; the codomain $\mathbb Z[t]$ and the degree bound are declared, not derived.

references.title: Liviu Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory (2nd ed.), Chapter 2 Section 2.3, printed pp. 46-53 (PDF pp. 56-63)

items.title: Poincare polynomial of a space and of a pair over a field
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field ([[def-field]]) and let $(X,A)$ be a pair of spaces whose
relative singular homology $H_k(X,A;F)$
([[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]],
[[def-relative-singular-homology]]) is finite-dimensional over $F$
([[def-dimension]]) for every $k$ and vanishes for all sufficiently large $k$.
Write
$$b_k(X,A;F):=\dim_F H_k(X,A;F)$$
and define the **relative Poincare polynomial over $F$** by
$$P_{X,A}(t):=\sum_k b_k(X,A;F)\,t^k\in\mathbb Z[t].$$
When $A=\varnothing$, so that $H_k(X,\varnothing;F)=H_k(X;F)$, the polynomial
$P_X(t):=P_{X,\varnothing}(t)=\sum_k b_k(X;F)\,t^k$ is the **Poincare polynomial
of $X$ over $F$**.

Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), for a closed smooth $n$-manifold the hypotheses hold: all $b_k$ are finite and
vanish for $k>n$. The coefficients are the **$F$-Betti numbers** and generally
depend on $F$ when $H_*(X;\mathbb Z)$ has torsion.
items.strategy: The conditional definition forms a finite nonnegative-degree sum of finite dimensions; empty X and A=X give zero. The reader added the inherited AC_omega qualification and the empty-face adapted-Morse existence prerequisite to the closed-manifold finiteness claim, and corrected CW structure to a CW homotopy model. Exact dimension, relative-chain and existence statements were checked. No choice is needed to name the conditional coefficients; the finiteness assertion inherits AC_omega. The filtration finiteness argument is separately reviewed at the Morse identity.

items.title: Rank bookkeeping for a long exact sequence of finite-dimensional vector spaces
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field ([[def-field]]) and let
$$\cdots\to A_k\xrightarrow{\alpha_k} B_k\xrightarrow{\beta_k} C_k\xrightarrow{\gamma_k} A_{k-1}\to\cdots$$
be a long exact sequence of $F$-vector spaces
([[def-exact-sequence-and-short-exact-sequence-in-an-abelian-category]]),
indexed by the integers. Assume that $A_k$ and $C_k$ are finite-dimensional
over $F$ for every $k$ ([[def-dimension]]) and vanish for $k<0$ and for all
$k>N$, where $N$ is a fixed integer. Then the spaces $B_k$ are also
finite-dimensional and vanish for $k<0$ and $k>N$, and there is a unique
polynomial $Q(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{N}q_kt^k\in\mathbb Z[t]$ with $q_k\ge0$ for every
$k$ such that
$$P_A(t)+P_C(t)=P_B(t)+(1+t)Q(t),$$
where $P_A(t)=\sum_{k}(\dim_F A_k)t^k$ and similarly for $B,C$. Explicitly
$q_k=\dim_F\ker\alpha_k$, so that for every $k$
$$\sum_{i=0}^{k}(-1)^{k-i}\bigl(\dim_F A_i+\dim_F C_i-\dim_F B_i\bigr)=q_k\ge0,$$
and in particular $\dim_F B_k\le\dim_F A_k+\dim_F C_k$ for every $k$.
items.strategy: rank-bookkeeping. Maps alpha/beta/gamma now have names distinct from a/r/s dimensions. Finite image and kernel bases and finitely many lifts establish B finite before rank-nullity; then A+C-B=a_k+a_(k-1). Exactness from C_(N+1)=0 gives a_N=0; negative N gives all-zero spaces. Telescoping and the coefficient recurrence prove both the partial sums and uniqueness, including k<0 empty sums. Exact subspace, dimension-formula, rank-nullity and polynomial interfaces were read. No infinite choice is used.

items.title: Long exact sequence of a triple in singular homology
items.statement:
For spaces $B\subseteq A\subseteq X$ and every abelian group $G$ there is a long
exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(A,B;G)\to H_n(X,B;G)\to H_n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(A,B;G)\to\cdots,$$
where the first two maps are induced by inclusions and $\delta$ is the
connecting homomorphism of the degreewise short exact sequence
$$0\to C_\bullet(A,B;G)\to C_\bullet(X,B;G)\to C_\bullet(X,A;G)\to0$$
of relative singular chain complexes. Moreover $\delta$ factors as the
connecting map $H_n(X,A;G)\to H_{n-1}(A;G)$ of the pair $(X,A)$ followed by
the quotient map $H_{n-1}(A;G)\to H_{n-1}(A,B;G)$.
items.strategy: degreewise-quotient. The quotient sequence C(A)/C(B) -> C(X)/C(B) -> C(X)/C(A) is degreewise exact and commutes with the boundary. The ordinary complex LES applies. Lifting the same relative cycle c in both sequences gives boundary dc, so the triple connector is the pair connector followed by quotient. Empty B recovers absolute H(X,B), rather than making H(X,A) absolute; the reader corrected that false remark. A=B and A=X degeneracies agree with zero quotient complexes. Exact chain and connector suppliers were opened.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Sections 2.1-2.2 (relative homology and long exact sequences)

items.title: A product collar deformation retracts onto its face
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary) and let
$C=M\times[0,1]$ be a product collar with face $M_0=M\times\{0\}$ (the
restriction of a smooth collar,
[[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]]). Then the projection
$$r:C\to M_0,\qquad r(x,t):=(x,0),$$
is a strong deformation retraction ([[def-retraction-and-deformation-retract]]),
and consequently for every abelian group $G$ and every $i$ the relative homology
$H_i(C,M_0;G)$ vanishes: the map of pairs $r:(C,M_0)\to(M_0,M_0)$ induces
isomorphisms on relative homology
([[def-relative-singular-homology]]).
items.strategy: explicit-formulas. The old (x,st) formula has reversed endpoints. Current H((x,t),s)=(x,(1-s)t) starts at identity, ends at r and fixes the face, including empty M. Pair naturality plus the five-term window supplies the relative isomorphism from four absolute isomorphisms; the target relative chain complex is zero. Exact retraction, homotopy invariance, pair LES, naturality and five-lemma statements match these uses.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Sections 2.1-2.2 (relative homology and long exact sequences)

items.title: The dual handle retraction onto the cocore, with the outgoing region carried onto the belt sphere
items.statement: For the standard $n$-dimensional $k$-handle $H=D^k\times D^{n-k}$ (, ) with core $K=D^k\times\{0\}$, cocore $C=\{0\}\times D^{n-k}$, attaching region $S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}$, attaching sphere $S^{k-1}\times\{0\}$, outgoing region $R=D^k\times S^{n-k-1}$ and belt sphere $B=\{0\}\times S^{n-k-1}$: (a) The formula $H_s(x,y):=(x,(1-s)y)$ defines a strong deformation retraction of $H$ onto the core $K$  that maps the attaching region into itself and maps it onto the attaching sphere at $s=1$. (b) The formula $G_s(x,y):=((1-s)x,y)$ defines a strong deformation retraction of $H$ onto the cocore $C$ that maps the outgoing region $R$ into itself and maps it onto the belt sphere $B$ at $s=1$. (c) $R\smallsetminus B$ strongly deformation retracts onto $S^{k-1}\times S^{n-k-1}$ by the radial map $(x,y)\mapsto(x/|x|,y)$, and this retraction fixes $S^{k-1}\times S^{n-k-1}$ pointwise.
items.strategy: Both retractions are explicit. For the first, retract $D^k$ onto $\{0\}\cup S^{k-1}$ by $x\mapsto\varphi_s(x)$ with $\varphi_s$ the radial strong deformation retraction that pushes every point of radius $\le 1$ to radius $\min(|x|,1-s)$; rescaling the radius so that the collar $S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}$ is fixed gives the deformation retraction of $H$ onto its cocore union outgoing region, fixing $D^k\times S^{n-k-1}$. The second is the deformation retraction of the punctured disk obtained by normalizing the $D^k$ factor, which is the identity on $S^{k-1}\times S^{n-k-1}$. This is the dual of Wall's handle retraction onto the core and attaching region (Milnor's deformation retraction $V\cup(D_R-q)\to V$ in the proof of his Lemma 6.3). Countable choice is not used: both deformations are formulas.

items.title: One handle changes relative homology in one degree only
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $F$ be a field.

(a) Let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let
$N'=N\cup_\varphi h^k$ be obtained by attaching a rounded $k$-handle along an
embedding $\varphi:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial N$
([[def-attaching-a-smooth-handle-with-corner-rounding]],
[[def-k-handle-core-cocore-attaching-region-and-belt-sphere]]). Then
$H_i(N',N;F)=0$ for $i\ne k$ and $H_k(N',N;F)\cong F$; the relative class of
the core disk $D^k\times\{0\}$ is a generator, and the connecting homomorphism
$\delta:H_k(N',N;F)\to H_{k-1}(N;F)$ of the pair carries it to the class of the
attaching sphere $\varphi(S^{k-1}\times\{0\})$ (up to the fixed sign of the
boundary operator).

(b) Let $f$ be smooth on a boundaryless manifold and let $a<b$ be regular
values with $f^{-1}([a,b])$ compact
([[def-closed-sublevel-and-level-set-of-a-smooth-function]]). If every critical
point in $f^{-1}([a,b])$ is nondegenerate and all of them have one common value
$c\in(a,b)$, then for every $i$
$$\dim_F H_i(M^b,M^a;F)=\#\{p\in f^{-1}([a,b]):\operatorname{ind}(p)=i\},$$
and the relative classes of the core disks of the attached handles form a
basis.
items.strategy: excision-and-good-pairs. Current good-pair proof handles k=0 separately by disjoint chains, so it never invokes the nonempty good-pair supplier with empty A. For k>0 the radial collar V contains every point of N, is open in the pushout, and fixes its seam; Y/N and H/A have identical quotient topologies. Pair homotopies preserve relative chains by the prism formula. The one-critical and simultaneous-handle arguments were read fully: pushed-in lower collars provide the pair comparison, while zero handles split off. Standard-pair core generators and connector dc give the attaching sphere, including terminal-minus-initial at k=1 and zero at k=0. A regular band retracts by collar compression; its inclusion is not a diffeomorphism. Reader repaired the empty-hypothesis and false-inclusion issues completely.

items.title: Attaching handles of index at least q preserves homology below q-1
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, let $F$ be a field, and let $q$ be an integer. Let $W'$ be obtained from a
smooth manifold $W$ with boundary by successively attaching finitely many
rounded handles of indices at least $q$
([[def-attaching-a-smooth-handle-with-corner-rounding]]). Then
$H_i(W',W;F)=0$ for every $i\le q-1$. Consequently the inclusion
$W\to W'$ induces isomorphisms $H_i(W;F)\to H_i(W';F)$ for $i\le q-2$ and a
surjection for $i=q-1$.
items.strategy: induction-on-handles. A 1-handle joining two components refutes the former injectivity claim at q-1=0. Current triple induction makes H_i(Wprime,W)=0 for i<=q-1; the pair LES gives isomorphisms only at i<=q-2 and surjectivity at q-1, with kernel image from H_q(Wprime,W). All endpoints including q<=0 and zero handles are consistent with negative-degree zero groups. Exact supplier statements checked. The owned chain-complex consumer F4 already uses the corrected surjection; outside direct consumers require Step 5b review.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Sections 2.1-2.2 (relative homology and long exact sequences)
Ralph L. Cohen, Bundles, Manifolds, and Homotopy, Chapter 12 Section 5, printed pp. 489-493 (PDF pp. 501-505)

items.title: Morse polynomial identity
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold
([[def-compact-space]]), let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be a Morse function and let $F$
be a field ([[def-field]]). Then there is a unique polynomial
$Q(t)=\sum_{k\ge0}q_kt^k\in\mathbb Z[t]$ with $q_k\ge0$ for all $k$ such that
$$M_f(t)=P_{M,F}(t)+(1+t)Q(t).$$
Equivalently, for every $k$
$$\sum_{i=0}^{k}(-1)^{k-i}m_i(f)\ \ge\ \sum_{i=0}^{k}(-1)^{k-i}b_i(M;F),$$
with equality of the total alternating sums; here $M_f$ is the Morse polynomial
([[def-morse-numbers-and-morse-polynomial]]) and $P_{M,F}$ is the Poincare
polynomial over $F$ ([[def-poincare-polynomial-over-a-field]]), which is well
defined because all $b_k(M;F)$ are finite and vanish for $k>n$.
items.strategy: filtration-telescoping. The reader explicitly separates empty M before min/max. For nonempty M, finitely many isolated critical points give regular separating levels and compact slabs. Each slab has relative homology only in the handle indices. The rank lemma inductively proves all absolute Betti numbers finite and zero above n before P is used; summing its finite identities telescopes. Nonnegative q_i sum to Q, coefficient recurrence proves uniqueness, and partial sums telescope to q_k; evaluation at -1 gives Euler equality. Repeated critical values use disjoint simultaneous handles, and n=0 gives only zero handles. Exact finite-critical, one-level, LES and polynomial interfaces were opened.

references.title: Liviu Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory (2nd ed.), Chapter 2 Section 2.3, printed pp. 46-53 (PDF pp. 56-63)
Ralph L. Cohen, Bundles, Manifolds, and Homotopy, Chapter 12 Section 5, printed pp. 489-493 (PDF pp. 501-505)

items.title: Strong Morse inequalities
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the situation of the Morse polynomial identity
([[thm-morse-polynomial-identity]]), for every $k$
$$\sum_{i=0}^{k}(-1)^{k-i}m_i(f)\ \ge\ \sum_{i=0}^{k}(-1)^{k-i}b_i(M;F),$$
and the difference of the two sides equals the coefficient $q_k$ of the
correction polynomial $Q$; for $k\ge n$ the two sides are equal, the common
value being $(-1)^k\sum_i(-1)^im_i(f)=(-1)^k\sum_i(-1)^ib_i(M;F)$.
items.strategy: coefficient-comparison. The stabilized common alternating sum must carry (-1)^k; the former omission is refuted by odd/even k on a manifold with nonzero Euler sum. Current coefficient recurrence gives difference q_k>=0, and the finite-degree maximal-coefficient argument gives q_k=0 for k>=n. The weak form follows by adding adjacent nonnegative differences, not subtracting inequalities. Empty M, n=0 and k beyond n checked against the already reviewed polynomial identity and rank lemma.

references.title: Ralph L. Cohen, Bundles, Manifolds, and Homotopy, Chapter 12 Section 5, printed pp. 489-493 (PDF pp. 501-505)
Alexander Ritter, Morse Homology (Cambridge Part III lecture notes), Lecture 21, PDF pp. 96-101
C. T. C. Wall, Differential Topology, Sections 5.1-5.4, printed pp. 129-148 (PDF pp. 137-151)

items.title: Weak Morse inequalities
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the situation of the Morse polynomial identity
([[thm-morse-polynomial-identity]]), $m_k(f)\ge b_k(M;F)$ for every $k$; that
is, the number of critical points of index $k$ is at least the $k$-th Betti
number over $F$.
items.strategy: coefficient-comparison. The coefficient argument m_k-b_k=q_k+q_(k-1)>=0 is sound. The reader removed a misleading citation of the Euler-only example as evidence of strict weakness versus strong inequalities: that example satisfies the strong inequalities as well. The current remark states only the valid comparison of coefficient conditions, with negative degrees zero and empty M consistent.

items.title: Perfect Morse function over a field
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold, let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be a Morse
function and let $F$ be a field ([[def-field]]). Write $m_k(f)$ for the Morse
numbers and $M_f(t)$ for the Morse polynomial of $f$
([[def-morse-numbers-and-morse-polynomial]]), and $b_k(M;F)=\dim_F H_k(M;F)$
for the $F$-Betti numbers with Poincare polynomial $P_{M,F}(t)
=\sum_kb_k(M;F)t^k$ ([[def-poincare-polynomial-over-a-field]]).

Then $f$ is **$F$-perfect**, or **perfect over $F$**, when
$$m_k(f)=b_k(M;F)\qquad\text{for every }k,$$
equivalently $M_f(t)=P_{M,F}(t)$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]).

Perfectness is always understood with respect to a field: it may hold over one
field and fail over another when $H_*(M;\mathbb Z)$ has torsion. No orientation
of $M$ and no Morse-Smale condition is required by the definition.
items.strategy: The reader carries AC_omega from closed-manifold Betti finiteness into this definition. Coefficient equality is precisely polynomial equality in Z[t], including empty M with both polynomials zero; no existence, excellence, orientation, or Morse-Smale assertion is made. Exact Morse-number, field and polynomial definitions match the notation.

references.title: Liviu Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory (2nd ed.), Chapter 2 Section 2.3, printed pp. 46-53 (PDF pp. 56-63)
Michele Audin and Mihai Damian, Morse Theory and Floer Homology, Part I Chapter 4 Section 4.4, printed pp. 88-91 (PDF pp. 98-100)

items.title: Total critical point lower bound
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold, $f$ Morse and $F$ a field. Then $$\#\operatorname{Crit}(f)=\sum_{k=0}^nm_k(f)\ \ge\ \sum_{k=0}^nb_k(M;F)=P_{M,F}(1),$$ and equality holds if and only if $f$ is $F$-perfect.
items.strategy: Sum the weak Morse inequalities $m_k\ge b_k$ over $k$ and use $M_f(1)=\#\operatorname{Crit}(f)$; a sum of nonnegative differences $m_k-b_k$ vanishes exactly when each does, which is the definition of $F$-perfectness. This is the coarsest numerical obstruction supplied by the page.

references.title: Liviu Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory (2nd ed.), Chapter 2 Section 2.3, printed pp. 46-53 (PDF pp. 56-63)
Michele Audin and Mihai Damian, Morse Theory and Floer Homology, Part I Chapter 4 Section 4.4, printed pp. 88-91 (PDF pp. 98-100)

items.title: Relative Morse inequalities for a cobordism
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact collared triad
([[def-smooth-cobordism-triad-for-morse-theory]]) and let $f:W\to[0,1]$ be an
adapted Morse function with $f^{-1}(0)=M_0$, $f^{-1}(1)=M_1$, all critical
points interior and nondegenerate
([[def-morse-function-adapted-to-a-cobordism]]), and let $F$ be a field. Write
$$m^{\mathrm{rel}}_k(f):=\#\{p\in\operatorname{Crit}(f):\operatorname{ind}(p)=k\}.$$
Then there is a unique polynomial $Q(t)=\sum_kq_kt^k\in\mathbb Z[t]$ with
$q_k\ge0$ such that
$$\sum_km^{\mathrm{rel}}_k(f)t^k=P_{W,M_0}(t)+(1+t)Q(t),$$
where $P_{W,M_0}(t)=\sum_k\dim_FH_k(W,M_0;F)t^k$ is the relative Poincare
polynomial ([[def-poincare-polynomial-over-a-field]]). Equivalently,
$m^{\mathrm{rel}}_k(f)\ge b_k(W,M_0;F)$ for every $k$ and the strong alternating
partial-sum inequalities hold for the relative Betti numbers. No orientability
of $W$ and no Morse-Smale hypothesis is assumed.
items.strategy: relative-filtration-telescoping. The reader repairs the lower-dimensional W0=M0 stage by choosing a positive regular bottom collar. Boundary df!=0 and patched local df(Y)=1 fields give face product bands; empty faces have empty bands, and zero critical points gives the entire product. Interior bump separation preserves boundary and indices. I additionally specify the exact closed band f^{-1}([t_(i-1),t_i]) in Proof 2.2, avoiding any ambiguity about intrinsic interior that could retain M0 in the displayed slab, and print the supplier pair-homotopy qualification. The reviewed interior-slab/one-handle comparison computes successive relative groups; triple exact sequences and rank bookkeeping prove finite Betti numbers and telescope. Top compression fixes M0, and coefficient recurrence proves uniqueness and all numerical forms. Exact boundary partition, flow and finite-bump suppliers were read. No orientation or Morse-Smale hypothesis is needed. Statement unchanged.

items.title: The handle chain complex computes singular homology
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold, let
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ be a Morse function and let $F$ be a field. Then there are an
index-ordered finite handle presentation of $M$ with exactly $m_k(f)$ handles of
index $k$, and a chain complex $(C_\bullet,\partial_\bullet)$ of
finite-dimensional $F$-vector spaces, a **handle chain complex** of
$(M,f,F)$, such that:

(i) $C_k$ has a chosen basis in bijection with the $k$-handles, given
by the relative classes of their core disks, so $\dim_FC_k=m_k(f)$;

(ii) $\partial_k:C_k\to C_{k-1}$ is the boundary homomorphism of the triple of
successive handle stages $W_k\supseteq W_{k-1}\supseteq W_{k-2}$;

(iii) $\partial_{k-1}\partial_k=0$;

(iv) $H_k(C_\bullet)\cong H_k(M;F)$ for every $k$.

In particular $H_k(M;F)$ is finite-dimensional for every $k$ and vanishes for
$k>n$.
items.strategy: cellular-transposition. The current index-order construction preserves the original critical points/indices after affine rescaling and local value separation; finite cluster separation/interchange makes each equal-index block simultaneous. Pair concentration supplies oriented chosen core bases, not orientation-independent distinguished bases. Triple boundary factorization gives d^2=0. Above-stage vanishing implies injectivity of H_k(W_k)->C_k and of q_(k-1), hence ker d_k is the former image. Pair exactness at the next stage quotients by im d_(k+1), and handles of index >=k+2 stabilize H_k. The reader supplied the previously omitted injection conditions and corrected F4 to surjection. I additionally defined all out-of-range W_j (empty below zero, M above n) for well-typed endpoint triples and repaired the displayed exact window in 3.2 as flagged. Empty M, k=0 and k=n are now explicitly covered. Statement unchanged.

Liviu Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory (2nd ed.), Chapter 2 Section 2.3, printed pp. 46-53 (PDF pp. 56-63)

items.title: Morse Euler characteristic identity
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold and
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ a Morse function. Then
$$\sum_{p\in\operatorname{Crit}(f)}(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}(p)}=\chi(M),$$
where $\chi(M)$ is the Euler characteristic computed from a finite CW
model homotopy equivalent to $M$ ([[def-euler-characteristic-of-a-finite-cw-complex]]); the
Euler-Poincare formula makes it independent of the chosen structure and equal
to the alternating sum of the Betti numbers
([[thm-euler-poincare-formula-for-finite-cw-complexes]]). The identity is
independent of the coefficient field, and it holds for every closed smooth
manifold, orientable or not.
items.strategy: evaluation-at-minus-one. Reader correction uses a finite CW homotopy model, rather than asserting an unstated CW structure on M. The independently reviewed handle presentation has one cell per handle; the finite rational complex identity dim C_k=dim H_k+dim B_k+dim B_(k-1) cancels boundaries and proves chi(M)=sum(-1)^k b_k(Q) without an unstated integral-to-rational rank comparison. I added the exact homotopy-invariance supplier to F6/deps for independence of the chosen model. Polynomial evaluation at -1 and the rational field give the identity; arbitrary fields have the same alternating sum. Empty M, n=0 and nonorientability need no exceptions. Exact Euler-Poincare/cellular interfaces and current batch-1 supplier proofs were checked. Statement unchanged by this adjudicator.

items.title: Perfectness, vanishing correction, and vanishing handle boundaries
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold, let
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ be Morse, let $F$ be a field, let $Q$ be the correction
polynomial of the Morse polynomial identity and let $(C_\bullet,\partial_\bullet)$
be a handle chain complex of $(M,f,F)$. The following are equivalent:

(i) $f$ is $F$-perfect;

(ii) $Q=0$;

(iii) every handle boundary map vanishes, $\partial_k=0$ for all $k$
(equivalently $\dim_F\operatorname{im}\partial_{k+1}=0$ for all $k$).
items.strategy: rank-comparison. The equivalences are valid in both directions: perfectness gives (1+t)Q=0 and uniqueness, while Q=0 gives coefficient equality. Zero differentials give homology equal to chains; conversely m_k-b_k=rank d_k+rank d_(k+1), so perfectness forces every rank zero. All spaces are finite by the reviewed chain supplier and its subspace hypotheses, and negative/top degrees are zero. Reader corrects the false claim that torsion is invisible to every field: an integral entry such as 2 may vanish in characteristic two, as the reviewed projective example confirms. No identification with a trajectory-count Morse differential is asserted.

items.title: Handle boundary coefficients are attaching-belt intersection numbers
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $F$ be a field. Let $M$ be a closed smooth oriented $n$-manifold
with an index-ordered handle presentation in which every attaching sphere $A_i$
of a $(k+1)$-handle meets every belt sphere $B_j$ of a $k$-handle transversely
in the middle level $N_k=\partial_+W_k$, for $0\le k\le n-1$; the endpoint
conventions for $k=0$ and $k=n-1$ are those of the geometric cancelling-pair
definition ([[def-geometric-cancelling-handle-pair]]): for $k=0$ the belt sphere
of a $0$-handle is its whole boundary sphere and the attaching sphere of a
$1$-handle is a $0$-sphere; dually for $k=n-1$. Orient each core disk, orient its attaching sphere by the boundary rule, and
orient its belt sphere so that the core-coordinate normal orientation followed
by the belt orientation is the boundary orientation of $N_k$. Then, with these
compatible orientations ([[def-induced-boundary-orientation]]), the matrix of the
handle-chain boundary $\partial_{k+1}:C_{k+1}\to C_k$ in the bases of the core
classes of the $(k+1)$-handles and of the $k$-handles is given by the attaching-belt
intersection entries $(I(A_i,B_j))$ (with entries mapped from $\mathbb Z$ to the coefficient field) as in the matrix definition in its middle-index range
([[def-attaching-belt-intersection-matrix-of-adjacent-index-handles]]), and the same
entry formula at the endpoints: the
coefficient of $\partial_{k+1}e_i$ at $f_j$ is the oriented intersection number
of $A_i$ with $B_j$ in $N_k$. Without orientations the same identity holds over
$\mathbb Z/2$ with mod-two intersection numbers, and over a field of
characteristic different from two the oriented identity holds.
items.strategy: collapse-degree-identification. The reader repairs the wrong collapse direction by the actual map p_j(x,y)=[x] to the oriented core quotient, constant on the seam and other handles. It extracts the jth relative core coefficient. Its fibre at [0] is exactly A_i intersect B_j; transversality gives a local core-coordinate diffeomorphism, and the core-normal-first belt orientation makes its local degree equal the attaching-first intersection sign. The complete published finite-puncture and degree proofs were read, including n=1, singleton and empty fibre. Local excision over F2 counts each point once; no ambient orientation is needed there. At k=0 the interval connector is terminal-minus-initial, with arbitrary core/belt sign changes handled by the stated compatible orientations; k=n-1 is in the positive-degree argument. The restricted matrix definition is used only as an entry convention, not an assertion of endpoint/disconnected applicability. I corrected the Milnor locator to the full Lemma 7.2/Corollary 7.3 proofs, printed pp. 85-89, PDF pp. 90-94; those pages were read. Statement unchanged by this adjudicator.

items.title: Morse inequalities and perfectness depend on the coefficient field
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The weak and strong Morse inequalities, the Morse
polynomial identity, and perfectness all depend on the coefficient field: only
the Euler characteristic identity is coefficient independent
([[cor-morse-euler-characteristic-identity]]).

More precisely, for a fixed Morse function $f$ on a closed manifold the Morse
numbers $m_k(f)$ do not depend on $F$
([[def-morse-numbers-and-morse-polynomial]]), while the Betti numbers
$b_k(M;F)$ can change with $F$ when $H_*(M;\mathbb Z)$ has torsion
([[def-poincare-polynomial-over-a-field]]); hence a function may be perfect
over one field and not over another ([[def-perfect-morse-function-over-a-field]]).
The correction polynomial $Q$ of the identity
$M_f=P_{M,F}+(1+t)Q$ is the coefficientwise measure of the loss
([[thm-morse-polynomial-identity]]), and the Euler identity survives because
$\sum_k(-1)^kb_k(M;F)=\chi(M)$ for every field.
items.strategy: The reader replaces ambiguous reducing-mod-prime can kill/create Betti wording with the precise statement that changing characteristic can change boundary ranks and Betti numbers. The reviewed finite handle computation supplies this dependence; its geometric ranks m_k stay fixed, and the polynomial recurrence uniquely adjusts Q. Alternating Betti sums remain chi by the reviewed Euler identity. The projective-space example supplies an actual characteristic contrast; the remark asserts possible dependence, not a change on every manifold. No unproved integral-rational comparison is used.

items.title: The height function on a sphere is perfect
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge1$ let $h:S^n\to\mathbb R$, $h(x)=x_{n+1}$, be the height function on the unit sphere. Its only critical points are the two poles $\pm e_{n+1}$, nondegenerate of indices $0$ and $n$, so $M_h(t)=1+t^n$ and $\#\operatorname{Crit}(h)=2$. Over every field $F$, the published homology of spheres gives $b_0(S^n;F)=b_n(S^n;F)=1$ and $b_k(S^n;F)=0$ otherwise, hence $P_{S^n,F}(t)=1+t^n=M_h(t)$: the height function is $F$-perfect for every $F$, with correction polynomial $Q=0$, and every weak inequality is an equality. For $n=1$ this is the circle with one minimum and one maximum.
items.strategy: In the chart of a pole the height function is quadratic with Hessian of signature $(0,n)$ at the top and $(n,0)$ at the bottom, which gives the two indices; the published Morse lemma shows there are no other critical points, and the computation is the standard height function on the round sphere. The homology is the published reduced homology of spheres, read in unreduced form. Substituting into the Morse polynomial identity over $F$ gives equality, so $Q=0$ and perfectness follow. The example tests the endpoint indices $0$ and $n$ and the equality case of the correction polynomial. Countable Choice is inherited from the in-run handle-theory suppliers of the Morse polynomial identity.

items.title: A Morse function on the torus is perfect over every field
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On the two-dimensional torus
$T^2=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ ([[def-two-dimensional-torus]]) let
$$f(x,y)=\cos(2\pi x)+\cos(2\pi y).$$
Its critical points are the four points with coordinates in
$\{0,\tfrac12\}$, with Hessians
$\operatorname{diag}(-4\pi^2\cos(2\pi x),-4\pi^2\cos(2\pi y))$, so the indices
are $2$ at $(0,0)$, $1$ at $(0,\tfrac12)$ and $(\tfrac12,0)$, and $0$ at
$(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$: $M_f(t)=1+2t+t^2$. The index-ordered handle presentation
has one $0$-handle, two $1$-handles and one $2$-handle, and its handle chain
complex over any field $F$ has ranks $1,2,1$; the boundary coefficients are the
intersection numbers of attaching and belt spheres: each $1$-handle attaches
with two feet on the belt circle of the $0$-handle and the attaching circle of
the $2$-handle meets each belt $0$-sphere of a $1$-handle in two points, and in
both cases the two contributions have opposite signs (and cancel mod two), so
$\partial_1=\partial_2=0$. Hence $H_0\cong F$, $H_1\cong F^2$, $H_2\cong F$ and
$P_{T^2,F}(t)=1+2t+t^2=M_f(t)$: $f$ is $F$-perfect for every field, and the
Euler identity gives $1-2+1=0=\chi(T^2)$.
items.strategy: direct-geometric-computation. Reader fixes the reversed indices: the cosine Hessian is negative at (0,0), positive at (1/2,1/2), and mixed at the other two points; gradient zeros exhaust all four. The 0/1/2 handle counts are 1/2/1. Endpoint signs cancel for the two feet of each 1-handle on the sole 0-handle. Just below the maximum the oriented surface has one disk removed; both sides of each untwisted band lie in that boundary and traverse its core in opposite directions. With compatible belt-point signs this gives two opposite intersection contributions for the cap, integrally and mod two. The reviewed endpoint coefficient lemma therefore yields both differentials zero, homology ranks 1/2/1, perfectness over every field, and Euler sum zero. The original runs-once description and pole indices were incorrect; the current geometric calculation is complete.

items.title: Real projective space shows coefficient-dependent perfectness
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Regard $\mathbb{RP}^n$ as the quotient of $S^n$ by
the antipodal map and let
$$f([x]):=\sum_{i=0}^n(i+1)x_i^2,$$
which is well defined because the squared coordinates are antipodally invariant.
Its critical points are the $n+1$ coordinate axes $[e_0],\dots,[e_n]$, of
indices $0,1,\dots,n$, so
$$M_f(t)=1+t+\cdots+t^n.$$
By the cellular homology of real projective space,
$b_k(\mathbb{RP}^n;\mathbb F_2)=1$ for $0\le k\le n$ (all boundary maps vanish
mod two), so $f$ is $\mathbb F_2$-perfect; over any field of characteristic
different from two, $b_0=1$, $b_k=0$ for $0<k<n$ and $b_n=1$ exactly when $n$
is odd, so for $n\ge2$ we get $b_1=0<1=m_1$ and $f$ is not perfect. For every
field the Euler identity holds: $\sum_k(-1)^k=1$ for even $n$ and $0$ for odd
$n$, which equals $\chi(\mathbb{RP}^n)$.
items.strategy: direct-computation. The original Hessian coefficient 2(j+1-i) is false and gives zero at j=i-1. Current quotient-chart expansion has coefficient 2(lambda_j-lambda_i)=2(j-i), with exactly i negatives and no zero. The tangent critical equation lambda_j x_j=mu x_j makes the axes exhaustive. The complete published cellular supplier was read: one cell per degree and differential 2 in positive even degrees, zero in odd degrees, with coefficient reduction through actual relative maps. Thus all F2 Betti numbers are one; other characteristics give H0=F, only odd top homology, and strict b1<m1 for n>=2. n=1 is perfect for all fields; Euler sum has the correct parity. Exact critical, cellular and perfectness interfaces match.

items.title: A created cancelling pair contributes a $(1+t)t^k$ term
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold with a
handle presentation, and let $M'$ be the presentation obtained by inserting a
geometrically cancelling pair of consecutive indices $k,k+1$ at an intermediate
stage ($0\le k\le n-1$), transporting the later attaching embeddings across the cancellation diffeomorphism and leaving their indices unchanged. Then $M'$ presents
the same manifold $M$; if $f$ and $f'$ are adapted Morse functions inducing the
two presentations, then
$$M_{f'}(t)=M_f(t)+t^k+t^{k+1}=M_f(t)+(1+t)t^k,\qquad P_{M',F}=P_{M,F},$$
and the correction polynomials satisfy $Q'=Q+t^k$. In the model case $M=S^2$
with the two-critical-point presentation $M_f(t)=1+t^2$, inserting a cancelling
$(0,1)$-pair gives $M_{f'}(t)=2+t+t^2$ and $Q'=1$.
items.strategy: presentation-comparison. The reader correctly invokes cancellation for an arbitrary given geometric pair, on its affected component, and transports later embeddings through the boundary diffeomorphism. The exact cancellation/creation and correspondence statements were checked, including k=0,n-1 and the nonempty outgoing-disc hypothesis of creation; existence of an insertion is not asserted on an empty outgoing face. Handle counts add t^k+t^(k+1), while diffeomorphism preserves all Betti numbers. I cite that preservation explicitly via homotopy invariance in F6/Proof 2.2, and apply polynomial uniqueness to the nonnegative candidate Q+t^k in Proof 3.1. Hence Qprime=Q+t^k, and the sphere model has 2+t+t^2, Qprime=1 and Euler sum two. Statement unchanged by this adjudicator.

items.title: Euler equality alone does not imply perfectness
items.statement:
**False claim:** for a Morse function on a closed smooth manifold the Euler
characteristic identity $\sum_p(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}(p)}=\chi(M)$ forces the
function to be perfect over every field, equivalently forces the correction
polynomial $Q$ of the Morse polynomial identity to vanish.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Start with the two-critical-point presentation of
$S^2$ (one $0$-handle and one $2$-handle, induced by the height function) and
insert a geometrically cancelling $(0,1)$-pair between them. The resulting
presentation has handles of indices $0,0,1,2$, and the corresponding Morse
function $f'$ on $S^2$ has Morse numbers $m_0=2$, $m_1=1$, $m_2=1$, so
$$M_{f'}(t)=2+t+t^2,\qquad \sum_k(-1)^km_k(f')=2-1+1=2=\chi(S^2).$$
Over every field, $P_{S^2,F}(t)=1+t^2$, hence $b_0=1<2=m_0$; the function is
not perfect over any field and its correction polynomial is $Q=1\ne0$. Thus the
Euler characteristic identity, which is an equality of alternating sums, does
not by itself force perfectness or the vanishing of $Q$.
items.strategy: explicit-construction. Reader uses creation at the disk stage, whose outgoing circle is nonempty and connected, and transports the final cap embedding by the supplied boundary diffeomorphism. Exact creation and correspondence suppliers were opened; the two new handles give counts 2/1/1 on the same sphere. Sphere Betti numbers 1/0/1 are valid over every field, so m0>b0 while the alternating sum stays two. Coefficient comparison gives Q=1; its correction (1+t)Q=1+t has excess in degrees zero and one, correcting the former false no-low-degree-excess remark. Deleting the pair restores the original presentation with unchanged homology. The false implication is therefore refuted for every field.
